:::{#thm-vcov-psd}
#### A variance matrix is symmetric and positive semidefinite

For a $p \times 1$ random vector $\vX = \tp{(X_1, \ldots, X_p)}$
with $\E{X_i^2} < \infty$ for every $i$,
$\Varf{\vX}$ is
[symmetric](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#def-symmetric-matrix)
and
[positive semidefinite](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/linear-algebra-special-matrices.html#def-positive-semidefinite):
for every $p \times 1$ vector of constants $\va$,

$$\tp{\va} \Varf{\vX} \va \ge 0$$

:::

::: proof

By @thm-vcov-elements, the $(i,j)$-th element of $\Varf{\vX}$ is $\Covs{X_i}{X_j}$,
and by @def-cov, with $\mean_i = \E{X_i}$:

$$
\ba
\Covs{X_i}{X_j}
&= \E{(X_i - \mean_i)(X_j - \mean_j)}
&& \text{(definition of covariance)} \\
&= \E{(X_j - \mean_j)(X_i - \mean_i)}
&& \text{(multiplication of numbers is commutative)} \\
&= \Covs{X_j}{X_i}
&& \text{(definition of covariance)}
\ea
$$

so the $(i,j)$-th and $(j,i)$-th elements are equal,
and $\Varf{\vX}$ is symmetric.

For positive semidefiniteness, let $Y = \tp{\va}\vX$. Then:

$$
\ba
\tp{\va} \Varf{\vX} \va
&= \Var{Y}
&& \text{(variance of a linear combination)} \\
&= \E{(Y - \E{Y})^2}
&& \text{(definition of variance)} \\
&\ge 0
&& \text{(} (Y - \E{Y})^2 \ge 0 \text{)}
\ea
$$

The first step is @thm-var-lincom.
The last step holds
because a [random variable](random-variables.qmd#def-random-variable) that is never negative <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
has a non-negative [expectation](expectation.qmd#def-expectation):
in the [discrete](random-variables.qmd#def-discrete-rv) and [continuous](random-variables.qmd#def-continuous-rv) cases of the <!-- check-term-links: allow -->
[definition of expectation](expectation.qmd#def-expectation),
every term of the sum, or the integrand, is non-negative
(for the general case, see @billingsley1995probability).

:::
